newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER - SUKER HAT-TRICK PUTS REAL MADRID TOP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER - SUKER HAT-TRICK PUTS REAL MADRID TOP.

text.p: Real Madrid knocked Barcelona off the top of the Spanish first division on Sunday thanks to a hat-trick by Croatian international Davor Suker in a 4-2 win over Valencia.

With 32 points from 14 games, Real lead by one point after Barcelona's 2-1 defeat at Athletic Bilbao on Saturday. A further point behind Barcelona are Deportivo Coruna, 4-1 winners over struggling Logrones.
Suker, who had been severely affected by an allergic reaction earlier in the week, combined superbly with Dutch international Clarence Seedorf in Real's best performance of the season.

Yet coach Fabio Capello's side had to come from behind after a defensive mistake let Goran Vlaovic through, and Valery Karpin was on hand to knock home the rebound in the 12th minute when Vlaovic's shot hit a post.
But Real struck straight back with two goals in five minutes from Suker.
The first came when the Croat reached acrobatically to control a through ball from Seedorf before crashing a fine shot into the roof of the net.
Seedorf set up the second with a perfectly-weighted pass to Victor Sanchez, who found Suker with a cross that hit a defender and ballooned over goalkeeper Andoni Zubizarreta.
Suker completed his second hat-trick of the season 15 minutes after the break when a cunning back-heel by Seedorf set up Roberto Carlos, who found Suker completely unmarked.
Raul sealed the game with a superb lob over Zubizarreta, before Valencia pulled one back from the penalty spot in the dying minutes.
Both Deportivo Coruna and Logrones ended their respective goal droughts, but John Toshack's side put in their best performance of the season to run out easy winners.
Four points behind Deportivo are Real Betis, another side who hit top form to regain fourth place from Athletic Bilbao in an exciting 3-1 win over Tenerife.

Tenerife went ahead after 30 minutes, but Felipe Minambres picked up a yellow card for asking for the ball without calling a name, and the Tenerife midfielder was sent off shortly afterwards after committing another bookable offence.

Pier Cherubino equalised for the home side and two goals from Nigerian international Finidi George ensured Betis came back to secure victory after one of their opponents was sent off for the third successive weekend.
Racing Santander are seventh after a goalless draw at Espanyol, while another surprise outfit, Valladolid, are sixth ahead of Monday's game against champions Atletico Madrid, eighth with 21 points.
Sevilla travelled to Celta Vigo without injured Brazilian signing Bebeto and suffered a 4-2 defeat, leaving them sixth from bottom after being tipped for a UEFA Cup place.
Sevilla manager Jose Antonio Camacho said the result flattered his side and criticised his players' for their "apathy".
Hercules climbed off the bottom by beating Compostela 1-0 in their first win since the opening game of the season.
